title: Horizon and Provision
premise: Ulyana Ishikawa flies medicine and gossip into a river country the maps forgot, paying off her late father's debt to a mining syndicate one cargo run at a time. When an expedition upriver goes silent, she is coerced into finding it — and discovers the syndicate's true prize: a glacier-locked valley whose meltwater memory holds the region's only fresh water rights. Trapped by the monsoon with a leaking boat and a defector from the expedition named Sable, Ulyana must choose between erasing what she knows and claiming a belonging she never believed she deserved. The story ends at calving season: Ulyana burns the syndicate's claim ledger into the river, takes the compass that was never hers, and finally lands somewhere she means to stay.
about_author: Freya Voss is the pen name of a former bush pilot who logged six years in subarctic river country before trading a cockpit for a writing desk. She writes adventure fiction about people who live where the infrastructure ends and the weather decides everything.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, Debt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A dawn supply run introduces her world: a battered plane, a ledger of her father's debt, and passengers who trade rumors like currency. She learns an expedition called Meridian has gone quiet on the upper river. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she likes being invisible, and the rumor unsettles her.

chapters.title: The Compass That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback woven through a night of engine repairs: how her father's brass compass came to her, and why the syndicate's collector, Mr. Ansel, treats her with courtesy that feels like a leash. Beat: grief sharpened into resentment.

chapters.title: Ansel's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ansel arrives at her strip with a contract: fly the search party's gear to the last known coordinates of Meridian. Refusal means the debt comes due now. She signs. Beat: the trap closing gently, almost kindly.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, brief cutaways. Her charter: a hydrologist named Okonkwo, a syndicate fixer named Reyes, and crates they won't let her inspect. Tension in the cabin; she reads people by how they sit in turbulence. Beat: suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: Last Known Coordinates
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They find Meridian's basecamp burned, radios smashed deliberately, and one lifeboat missing. Reyes wants to log it as accident. Okonkwo quietly disagrees. Beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: Weather Window Closing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Monsoon fronts stack on the horizon. She argues for turning back; Ansel's voice on the radio orders them upriver by boat instead. The plane must stay behind. Beat: claustrophobia — the sky itself siding against her.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The chartered boat takes on water faster than the bilge can argue. Reyes reveals he can't swim, which changes the power dynamic. Beat: forced interdependence among strangers.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A figure hails them from a driftwood camp: Sable, Meridian's surveyor, half-starved, who claims the rest of the team went deeper into the valley 'voluntarily.' She lies badly about some things and perfectly about others. Beat: wary hope.

chapters.title: What Meridian Was Looking For
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback. The expedition's real mission: mapping the glacier-fed aquifer before calving season opens the route, so the syndicate can file exclusive water claims. Sable walked when she understood what the data would be used for. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Days pinned under rain in a cave camp; rations shrink; Reyes transmits coded updates on a hidden radio Ulyana finds. Beat: trust eroding in the damp.

chapters.title: The Hidden Radio
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Confrontation over the radio. Reyes admits Ansel ordered him to confirm Sable's location — dead or alive. Ulyana realizes she flew the leash in herself. Beat: betrayal, then cold clarity.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Maps
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. He shows Ulyana his own data: the aquifer feeds every settlement downriver. If the syndicate gates it, thousands lose water. He asks her not to fly out even if the weather breaks. Beat: the debt versus the common good made concrete.

chapters.title: River Country Memory
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At a drowned village site, Sable tells stories of the people who lived here before the dam failed decades ago — including, it turns out, Ulyana's father, who once ran this same river. Beat: belonging as inheritance, not geography.

chapters.title: My Father's River
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She confronts the truth: her father wasn't just a pilot in debt; he was a witness who hid evidence of the aquifer inside his old flight logs. The compass is a key to where they're cached. Beat: the past reorganizing the present.

chapters.title: Reyes Deserts
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Terrified and loyal to nothing but survival, Reyes steals the boat's fuel reserve and heads downriver to report. Beat: pity without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The trio races downstream on a raft of salvaged drums to intercept Reyes before he reaches the syndicate's relay station. Beat: adrenaline laced with futility.

chapters.title: The Relay Station
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They reach the station first and sabotage the transmitter, but Reyes arrives armed. A standoff in the rain; Okonkwo talks him down — barely. They maroon him with supplies. Beat: violence averted, not resolved.

chapters.title: Intermission of Rain
chapters.summary: Three-way POV. Weeks of waiting at the station. Small domesticities: mending nets, teaching each other card games, Sable and Ulyana circling something unspoken. Beat: tenderness growing in enforced stillness.

chapters.title: What Sable Buried
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She confesses she led Meridian to the cache site under duress before defecting; the syndicate may already have partial data. Her guilt mirrors Ulyana's debt. Beat: two liars trading honesty.

chapters.title: The Flight Logs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using the compass bearings, they locate the waterproof cache in a cliff fissure: her father's logs documenting the aquifer's extent and the syndicate's falsified surveys. Beat: awe and terror — paper heavier than any cargo.

chapters.title: Ansel Ascendant
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Ansel). In the lowland office, Ansel receives Reyes's garbled report and dispatches a gunboat upriver, timed to the calving window. Beat: patient, institutional menace.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The glacier begins to calve; the route through the gorge will be navigable for perhaps ten days. They must move the logs and themselves out before the ice closes or the gunboat arrives. Beat: the clock starting audibly.

chapters.title: Through the Gorge
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A white-knuckle passage between calving walls, icefall thunder, near-capsize. Sable saves Okonkwo from the water; Ulyana saves the logs and hates herself for the priority. Beat: fear exposing character.

chapters.title: The Gunboat Behind Them
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Smoke on the water behind — Ansel's boat entering the gorge against all sense. He'd rather lose men than the claim. Beat: being hunted by arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They rig a rockslide to block the narrows, gambling the gunboat turns back. It works, but Okonkwo is injured shielding Sable. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: Fever
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Okonkwo's wound infects; Ulyana flies no plane but improvises — boiled instruments, salvaged antibiotics from her old med runs. She keeps him alive through the night. Beat: the healer's identity she'd abandoned returning.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ansel
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ansel catches them at a fuel cache and offers the clean way out: hand over the logs, debt forgiven, strip and hangar returned. Ulyana asks for time. Beat: temptation wearing her own face.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable urges burning the logs — knowledge this dangerous gets people killed. Ulyana refuses: the settlements need proof, not ashes. Their first real fight. Beat: love and principle colliding.

chapters.title: Downriver Allies
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. They reach the delta settlements and find the rumors Ulyana carried for years were seeds: river families remember her father, and they will shelter the three fugitives. Beat: belonging arriving unasked.

chapters.title: The Council of Landings
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Settlement representatives meet in a fish-drying shed. Okonkwo, feverish but lucid, presents the aquifer data. They decide to file a collective counter-claim — but someone must deliver originals to the territorial registry before Ansel's lawyers. Beat: hope requiring risk.

chapters.title: Who Flies
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Only Ulyana can fly the registry run, but her plane sits at the syndicate strip, guarded. Sable volunteers to walk in and draw the guards. Beat: choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Theft of Wings
chapters.summary: Split POV. Sable's diversion — a fire in the fuel store; Ulyana's cold-blooded preflight and takeoff under rifle fire, a wingtip clipped but flying. Beat: triumph with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Registry
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The territorial clerk, bribed and frightened, resists filing. Ulyana produces her father's original survey stamps — his name still carries legal weight — and the counter-claim is lodged. Beat: inheritance converted into standing.

chapters.title: Ansel's Last Card
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Denied the claim, Ansel pivots to theft: if he can't own the water, he'll destroy the evidence and the witnesses. He charters his own aircraft. Beat: corruption shedding its last politeness.

chapters.title: Storm Intercept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flying back through the monsoon's tail, Ulyana spots Ansel's plane and forces a cat-and-mouse in cloud, using river fog she's flown since girlhood. His aircraft ditches; he survives. Beat: mastery earned, mercy chosen.

chapters.title: What Ansel Confesses
chapters.summary: Two-hander scene, Ulyana and Ansel on the shingle. Wet, defeated, he admits the debt was fabricated to control her father — and that her father died running evidence, not fleeing shame. Beat: rage transmuting into release.

chapters.title: Ledger into River
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Before witnesses at the delta landing, Ulyana burns the syndicate's claim ledger page by page into the current — not destroying law, but ending the fiction of her family's guilt. Beat: catharsis, grief finally warm.

chapters.title: Calving Ends
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The gorge ices shut behind them; the route closes until next year. Sable chooses to stay through the winter rather than return south. She and Ulyana stop pretending the circling is accidental. Beat: quiet, unglamorous love.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Cargo
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Repaired wing, new paint, a manifest of medicine and mail — no debts attached. She flies the settlements' winter run with Sable navigating beside her. Beat: work restored as joy.

chapters.title: Horizon and Provision
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, coda. On a clear dawn she sets the brass compass on the dashboard, needle steady, and banks toward the interior — visible now, named now, staying. Final beat: invisibility traded for belonging, freely chosen.
